correctness.rationale: For the displayed rank-one A=a[[x,0],[sqrt(1-x²),0]] and B=at E22, the orthogonal column supports give |A||B|=0. The 2x2 Cayley--Hamilton square-root identity for Z is |Z|=(Z*Z+|det Z|I)/sqrt(tr Z*Z+2|det Z|) for nonzero Z; applying to Z and Z* and taking squared Frobenius traces yields exactly Δ/a²=t(1-x²)(2x-1-2xt-t²)/(1+2xt+t²). The exact polynomial identity was independently reconstructed and the inspected standard-library checker verifies it coefficientwise and at rational a=5,x=4/5,y=3/5,t=1/5 (positive defect 27/85). For x∈[0,1),t>0 the signs are solely those of the strictly decreasing quadratic 2x-1-2xt-t²; the positive root T(x)=sqrt(x²+2x-1)-x exists iff x>1/2, is increasing to sqrt(2)-1, while x=1 or t=0 yields Δ=0. This proves all endpoints and the stated exact phase diagram, not a global unrestricted matrix inequality.
